content.text:
After scanning the open list, I agree that #156 is probably not the best next move. It improves the machinery for future agents, but it doesn’t create a player-facing win.

My strongest candidates are:

1. [#158 — Hydraulics showcase](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/158) — best immediate implementation. It is bounded, uses existing mechanics, and produces a concrete discovery moment. `GRAVITY-3`, but the issue already supplies strong technical scaffolding for LUNA medium.

2. [#161 — Monster item-use AI](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/161) — smallest, safest player-facing slice. It validates existing AI behavior, canonical item transfer, and tactical counterplay. `GRAVITY-2`.

3. [#157 — Mechanic surfacing audit](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/157) — best if we want evidence before committing. It can quickly identify which existing mechanic has the highest payoff and prevent us from building a showcase around something unreachable or silent.

I’d defer these for now:

- [#170 — World exploration](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/170): excellent direction, but a large coordination umbrella.
- [#171 — Leveling](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/171): compelling, but introduces a new persistent progression contract.
- [#163 — Corpse adaptations](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/163): valuable, but has a substantial discovery/persistence/UI surface.
- [#166 — Town contracts](https://github.com/PJensen/JSHack/issues/166): economy-to-quest coupling makes it riskier.
- [#172 — Stat scaling research](https://github.com/PJensen/JSHack/issues/172): useful research, but not the next player-visible improvement.
- [#159 — Discovery-first pattern](https://github.com/PJensen/JSHack/issues/159): explicitly wants #158 proven first.

My suggested sequence is:

`#157 audit → #158 hydraulics slice → #161 AI slice → #159 pattern extraction`

If we want to start implementing immediately, I’d pick #158.
I just felt like skills would HELP with continued development.

Yes—that’s a good instinct. Skills work is infrastructure for making every subsequent issue faster and safer, especially with LUNA medium.

My concern is only that #156’s full scope is too broad as the immediate task. A better approach would be:

- Work on a concrete issue such as #158 or #161.
- Capture the real authoring path, test workflow, and common pitfalls.
- Make a focused update to the relevant skill afterward.
- Expand toward #156 incrementally as patterns are proven.

That gives us immediate gameplay progress while turning each completed issue into better guidance for continued development.
it's almost like we want to updated AGENTS.md to perform skill capture as we're going -- incrementally

Exactly. Rather than treating #156 as one large documentation project, `AGENTS.md` could make skill capture part of the normal delivery loop:

1. Before work: identify whether the issue exposes a reusable workflow.
2. During work: record canonical files, commands, invariants, and failure modes.
3. After work: update or create the smallest relevant skill.
4. Validate the skill against the completed implementation.
5. Keep broad coverage work incremental and evidence-based.

The key rule would be: capture proven practice, not speculative architecture.

That turns every gameplay issue into two outputs:

- the feature itself;
- a better starting point for the next LUNA session.

It also makes #156 a rolling objective rather than a prerequisite gate.
Approving this pre-GREENLIGHT work item, there are many buried tools, processes and best practices all over this project.

I’ll turn that approval into a focused `AGENTS.md` rule: capture reusable tools, processes, and best practices incrementally as each issue is implemented, without making the broad skills audit a prerequisite.

Yes. The distinction is valuable:

- Deterministic tools capture repeatable discovery, validation, audits, and evidence.

`AGENTS.md` should explicitly say to capture both. That reflects what you’re building at work: agents get better not just from instructions, but from reliable tools that reduce guessing and produce inspectable results.

Suggested wording:

> When a task reveals a reusable skill or deterministic tool—a command, audit, lookup, fixture, validator, or report generator—capture it incrementally after the pattern is proven. Skills explain how to reason and work; tools make recurring checks repeatable and evidence-based.

This would be a worthwhile follow-up commit, especially since the current project already has tools like `agent-target`, `content-id-audit`, `event-bus-explorer`, and `system-map`.
I would --- in fact, I'd start organizing the existing tooling along these lines, my mental model is cloudflare wrangler skills -- they're fantastic.

That’s the right mental model. Organize around agent workflows, not around the historical location of scripts.

A Wrangler-style structure would be:

- `skill`: when to use it, reasoning workflow, constraints, and interpretation.
- `tool`: deterministic command that gathers evidence or performs a bounded check.
- `AGENTS.md`: routing table that tells agents which skill/tool to use.
- tests: verify the tool’s output and the architectural invariant it protects.

For JSHack, the first natural domains are:

- architecture and health
- event topology
- scheduler/system mapping
- content and ID tracing
- deterministic simulation audits
- target lookup
- provenance and intent through Entire

The existing tools already contain most of the raw material. The work is primarily giving them stable agent-facing contracts, consistent output modes, and discoverable skills—incrementally, as each workflow is used.

That would make “find the right way to work” feel much more like Wrangler: intent first, reliable command surface second, implementation details only when needed.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md
+---
+name: agent-tools
+description: Use JSHack's deterministic inspection and architecture tools to locate behavior, verify boundaries, and gather evidence before changing code.
+argument-hint: <question-or-target>
+---
+
+Use this skill when a task needs repository-wide discovery, architecture evidence,
+event wiring analysis, scheduler mapping, content-ID tracing, or a health check.
+These tools are read-only unless a command explicitly says otherwise. Prefer the
+smallest tool and output mode that answers the question.
+
+## Start with the question
+
+Choose the route before searching broadly:
+
+| Need | Tool | First command |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Find a symbol, event, file, or test | `agent-target` | `deno run --allow-read tools/agent-target.mjs TERM --limit 80` |
+| Trace an item, monster, spell, material, loot, or visual ID | `content-id-audit` | `deno run --allow-read tools/content-id-audit.mjs ID --limit 80` |
+| Understand event producers and consumers | `event-bus-explorer` | `deno run --allow-read tools/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format summary --top 40` |
+| Inspect one event contract | `event-bus-explorer` | `deno run --allow-read tools/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event EVENT` |
+| Map scheduler registration and phases | `system-map` | `deno run --allow-read tools/system-map.mjs --format summary` |
+| Find unregistered or untested systems | `system-map` | `deno run --allow-read tools/system-map.mjs --unregistered` or `--missing-tests` |
+| Check architecture hazards | `agent-health` | `deno run --allow-read tools/agent-health.mjs` |
+| Inspect import-layer violations | `import-boundary-report` | `deno run --allow-read tools/import-boundary-report.mjs` |
+
+## Evidence workflow
+
+1. Run the narrowest relevant command before reading unrelated source.
+2. Follow tool results to the named files, systems, tests, or event contracts.
+3. Check scheduler registration and layer boundaries when the change crosses
+   rules, bridge, display, or main.
+4. Check event producers and consumers when adding or changing an event.
+5. Use `content-id-audit` before changing content-facing definitions so every
+   canonical reference and presentation path is known.
+6. Run `deno test --allow-read tests/agentTools.test.mjs` if tool behavior or
+   parsing assumptions change.
+
+## Useful output modes
+
+- `summary` is for a fast human scan.
+- `csv` is for exact producer/consumer or reference inspection.
+- `mermaid` is for visualizing event relationships.
+- `--producer-only` and `--consumer-only` expose orphaned event wiring.
+- `--phase`, `--unregistered`, and `--missing-tests` focus the system map.
+
+## Guardrails
+
+- Treat reports as evidence, not as permission to delete apparently unused
+  files. Listener installers and dynamic references can be intentionally absent
+  from static registration results.
+- Keep tool changes deterministic, import-safe, and usable with `--allow-read`.
+- Extend existing tools when a question recurs; do not add a one-off grep script
+  for a query they can already answer.
+- When a new recurring workflow is proven, update this skill with the route and
+  validation command rather than creating duplicate guidance elsewhere.
+
+## Related project tasks
+
+```bash
+deno task guard:architecture
+deno task guard:events
+deno task guard:tools
+deno task audit:health
+deno task audit:events
+deno task audit:systems
+```
+
*** Update File: /home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/AGENTS.md
@@

@@
 `content-id-audit` follows item, monster, spell, material, loot, visual, and
 test references by ID.
+
+For the complete routing workflow, use
+[`.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md).
@@
 ### Content-First Engine Work
*** End Patch";
